title: Neo-Assyrian relief from Nimrud
studyNote: Material culture from ancient Kalhu, commonly identified with biblical Calah. It provides historical and geographic context for the Assyrian world named in Scripture; it does not by itself prove a particular biblical event.
teachingPrompt: Use alongside a map to distinguish Calah/Nimrud, Nineveh, and Babylon.

title: Cavalry relief from Nineveh
object: Relief fragment: cavalryman leading his horse beside a stream
studyNote: A Nineveh relief from the reign-period of Sennacherib gives direct material context for the Assyrian capital and military world described in Kings and Nahum. The object establishes setting and period, not every detail of those passages.
teachingPrompt: Compare the imperial strength pictured here with the limits God placed upon Sennacherib in 2 Kings 19.
rights: CC0 / Met Open Access; object API reports isPublicDomain true.

title: Lion panel from Nebuchadnezzar's Babylon
studyNote: This glazed architectural panel comes from Babylon during Nebuchadnezzar II's reign. It supplies tangible visual context for the city and royal age in which Judah's exile and the opening chapters of Daniel are set.
teachingPrompt: Use the image to introduce Babylon's scale and royal imagery before reading the KJV passage.
